newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka Jan-Sept tourist arrivals down 30 pct.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka Jan-Sept tourist arrivals down 30 pct.

text.p: Tourist arrivals to Sri Lanka fell 30 percent in the first nine months of 1996 from a year earlier, the Ceylon Tourist Board said on Tuesday.
The tropical island recorded 218,004 arrivals in January-September, down from 312,132 in the same 1995 period, a report published by the board said.

Industry sources say tourist arrivals plummeted soon after separatist Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam guerrillas blew up Colombo's Central Bank in January, killing more than 80 people and destroying part of the city's financial district.
Sri Lanka, which relies on tourism as a major source of foreign exchange income and employment, recorded 403,101 tourist arrivals last year.

The Sri Lankan government has said it planned to launch a multi-milion dollar advertising campaign in its major tourist markets in Europe and in the Far East to stress the 13-year ethnic war is largely limited to the country's north and east.
